text_blocks.snippet: High blood pressure (hypertension) is officially diagnosed when your blood pressure readings are consistently at or above 130/80 mm Hg.

Blood pressure is measured using two numbers: systolic (the top number, measuring pressure when the heart beats) and diastolic (the bottom number, measuring pressure when the heart rests between beats).
Blood pressure ranges from the American Heart Association and CDC are categorized as follows:

list.snippet: Elevated: 120–129 systolic and less than 80 diastolic
Hypertensive Crisis: Higher than 180 systolic and/or higher than 120 diastolic

text_blocks.snippet: What to Do If Your Numbers Are High

list.snippet: Stage 1 or 2: Consult a doctor, as a single reading isn't a definitive diagnosis. Providers evaluate patterns over time or home monitoring.
Above 180/120 mm Hg: Retest after five minutes. If readings remain high with symptoms like chest pain, shortness of breath, or weakness, call 911. Without symptoms, contact your doctor immediately.
